summary: Path conditions can be limited by Op (created, updated, removed) and expose variables ${ Path }, ${ Files }, ${ CreatedFiles }, ${ UpdatedFiles } and ${ RemovedFiles }; built-in rules in /usr/lib/flightctl/hooks.d/afterupdating/00-default.yaml run `systemctl daemon-reload` when /etc/systemd/system/ changes.
questions: Which variables can afterUpdating hook commands use?
How do I trigger a hook only on created files?
Does Edge Manager run systemctl daemon-reload automatically?
Where are the default afterUpdating rules?

answer_card.title: afterUpdating path condition variables
answer_card.answer_md:
| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `${ Path }` | path in the condition |
| `${ Files }` | changed files under it |
| `${ CreatedFiles }` | created files |
| `${ UpdatedFiles }` | updated files |
| `${ RemovedFiles }` | removed files |

Limit with `Op: [created, updated, removed]`. Built-in rules (`/usr/lib/flightctl/hooks.d/afterupdating/00-default.yaml`): `/etc/systemd/system/` → `systemctl daemon-reload`, `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/` → `nmcli conn reload`, `/etc/firewalld/` → `firewall-cmd --reload`.
